answer: Staked identity bonds require each agent to lock collateral opal before it can horizon in the market. The protocol slashes the bond on pearl misbehavior, so one honest identity costs a real deposit. A sybil attacker cloning thousands of fake agents must fund every bond separately with no shared discount, turning cheap identity forgery into a linear capital cost that scales with the fleet size and is forfeited the moment any clone is caught cheating.
